analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md was supplied. Base lines 1381-1756 are historical release notes with no head-side change visible in this slice. The head excerpt (lines 1-239) adds notes, and no source code was provided, so claimed behavior is unverified.

Security-relevant claims in the head text:
- New Autopilot daily earnings floor, funded from a separate pool, with admin inspect/fund/repair endpoints (lines 3-13). It touches A-009, TB-006 and T-055. The finding above covers the missing threat coverage.
- Machine-scoped Autopilot desired mode stored in the database, with grants revoked on revision (lines 19-24).
- Soft-delete mutation gate defaulting to false (line 87).
- Account erasure with grace period and outbox (lines 93-111). This maps to T-059, and the existing definitions seem to cover it.
- Logs stop writing personal data (line 119).
- Top-level user, metadata and similar fields removed from provider-bound bodies (line 239). This matches the canonical context.
- Migration timeouts and early trust preflight (lines 82-87).
- Admin machine diagnostics that expose reported pins and resident models (line 17).
- Prefix-cache SSD write-budget ledger (line 52). T-041 remains consistent: HMAC names, 30-minute TTL and a disk budget.
- Bedrock review and merge clearance (lines 36-44).

The next pass should verify the actual coordinator and ledger code for Autopilot rewards. Key checks are server-authenticated consent and uptime evidence, per-account and per-machine caps, the idempotence of pool funding, and admin-endpoint authorization.

findings.detail: The changelog describes a new funded daily top-up to 110% of a baseline. For machines with under seven days of history, the baseline is a cohort average. Qualification needs only macOS 27 or later, two downloaded models, saved consent and 90% uptime. Sessions and identity aliases are merged, but the entry does not show that the top-up depends on served inference, or that the machine is a unique physical Mac. T-055 already says App Attest aliases prove credential continuity, not unique hardware or capacity. An operator (ADV-001) could therefore register many fresh or low-traffic machines, or machines running on borrowed identities, keep them connected, and draw cohort-based floor payments from the shared pool until the cap is reached. The pool cap bounds the loss. Uptime, model-inventory and consent inputs come from provider reports or the provider-authenticated socket. The new admin funding, repair and backfill endpoints also touch A-009 and TB-006. No threat entry covers reward-fraud, cohort-baseline gaming or these admin controls. Fix: add a threat entry for payout abuse and its mitigations. Before enabling payments, consider requiring minimum served-token or work evidence, per-account and per-machine caps, a cohort minimum size, and an audit trail for backfill and repair.
findings.title: Autopilot earnings floor adds a payout path that the threat model does not cover (sybil and self-reported uptime)
